drivingQuestion: Does the mishna show that contemplation is tantamount to speech, and why is the impure man told to contemplate?
outcomeNote: The closing אלא settles why prayer alone is exempted, but the dispute between Ravina and Rav Ḥisda over whether contemplation is tantamount to speech is left unadjudicated.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רָבִינָא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי. דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי — לָמָּה מְהַרְהֵר?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Ravina said: That is to say,» from the mishna that «contemplation is tantamount to speech. As if it would enter your mind» that «it is not tantamount to speech,» then «why» does one who is impure because of a seminal emission «contemplate?» It must be that it is tantamount to speech.

segments.he: אֶלָּא מַאי — הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי, יוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו?
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this: «But what» are you saying, that «contemplation is tantamount to speech?» Then, if one who is impure because of a seminal emission is permitted to contemplate, why does he not «utter» the words «with his lips?»

The Gemara answers: «As we found at» Mount «Sinai.» There one who had sexual relations with a woman was required to immerse himself before receiving the Torah, which was spoken and not merely contemplated. Here, too, it was decreed that one who was impure due to a seminal emission may not recite matters of Torah out loud until he immerses himself.

segments.he: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר, הִרְהוּר לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי — יוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו.
segments.en: «And Rav Ḥisda said» that the opposite conclusion should be drawn from the mishna: «Contemplation is not tantamount to speech, as if it would enter your mind» that «contemplation is tantamount to speech,» then one who is impure because of a seminal emission should ab initio, «utter» Shema «with his lips.»

segments.he: אֶלָּא מַאי הִרְהוּר לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי, לָמָּה מְהַרְהֵר? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ כׇּל הָעוֹלָם עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ וְהוּא יוֹשֵׁב וּבָטֵל.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this argument: «But what» are you saying, that «contemplation is not tantamount to speech?» If so, «why does he contemplate? Rabbi Elazar said: So that» a situation «will not» arise «where everyone is engaged in» reciting Shema «and he sits idly» by.

segments.he: וְנִגְרוֹס בְּפִרְקָא אַחֲרִינָא! אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: If that is the only purpose, «let him study another chapter» and not specifically Shema or one of the blessings. «Rav Adda bar Ahava said:» It is fitting that one engage «in a matter in which the community is engaged.»

segments.he: וַהֲרֵי תְּפִלָּה, דְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר עֲסוּקִין בּוֹ, וּתְנַן: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי — לֹא יַפְסִיק, אֶלָּא יְקַצֵּר. טַעְמָא דְּאַתְחֵיל, הָא לָא אַתְחֵיל — לֹא יַתְחִיל!
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «And prayer,» which is also «a matter in which the community is engaged, and we learned» in the mishna: «One who was standing in prayer and remembered that he is one» who experienced «a seminal emission» and did not yet immerse himself «should not interrupt» his prayer, «rather he should abridge it.» The Gemara infers: «The reason is because he» already «began» to pray; «however,» if «he did not» yet «begin,» then «he should not begin,» even by means of contemplation.

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי תְּפִלָּה דְּלֵית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם. וַהֲרֵי בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאַחֲרָיו דְּלֵית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, וּתְנַן עַל הַמָּזוֹן מְבָרֵךְ לְאַחֲרָיו וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ לְפָנָיו! אֶלָּא: קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וּתְפִלָּה דְּרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Prayer is different» in «that it does not contain» the acceptance of the yoke of «the kingdom of Heaven.» The Gemara rejects this: «And Grace after Meals does not contain» the acceptance of the yoke of «the kingdom of Heaven, and» yet «we learned» in the mishna: «Over food, one recites a blessing afterward, but does not recite a blessing beforehand. Rather,» the differences must be explained otherwise: «The recitation of Shema and Grace after Meals» are both mitzvot «by Torah law, while prayer» is only «by rabbinic law.» Therefore, one who is impure need not pray.

moves.summary: infers from the mishna of the preceding unit that contemplation equals speech
moves.about: since the impure man contemplates Shema, contemplation must be tantamount to speech

moves.summary: if so, let him utter the words with his lips
moves.about: if contemplation equals speech, the impure man should simply utter the words with his lips

moves.summary: utterance is barred on the precedent of Sinai
moves.about: utterance is barred by the precedent of Sinai, where those impure separated before the Torah was spoken

moves.summary: draws the opposite conclusion from the same mishna
moves.about: were contemplation equal to speech the impure man would utter Shema outright, so it is not

moves.summary: then why does the mishna have him contemplate at all
moves.about: if contemplation is not speech, why does the mishna have him contemplate at all

moves.summary: so that he not sit idle while everyone else is engaged
moves.about: he contemplates so as not to sit idle while everyone else is occupied with Shema

moves.summary: then let him study any other chapter
moves.about: if idleness is the whole concern, let him study some other chapter instead of Shema

moves.summary: it must be the matter the community is engaged in
moves.about: he should be occupied with the very matter the community is occupied with

moves.summary: objects from the mishna on prayer, which the community is engaged in yet he may not begin
moves.about: prayer too is a matter the community is engaged in, yet the impure man may not begin it

moves.summary: prayer lacks acceptance of the yoke of Heaven
moves.about: prayer is different in that it contains no acceptance of the yoke of Heaven

moves.summary: Grace after Meals lacks it too, yet the mishna permits it
moves.about: Grace after Meals also lacks acceptance of the yoke of Heaven, yet the mishna has the impure man recite it

moves.cueHe: אלא: קריאת שמע וברכת המזון דאורייתא
moves.summary: the line is Torah law against rabbinic law
moves.about: the true line is Torah law against rabbinic law — Shema and Grace after Meals are from the Torah, prayer is rabbinic

edges.cueHe: אמר רבינא: זאת אומרת הרהור כדבור דמי
edges.about: since the impure man contemplates Shema, contemplation must be tantamount to speech

edges.cueHe: אלא מאי — הרהור כדבור דמי, יוציא בשפתיו?
edges.about: if contemplation equals speech, the impure man should simply utter the words with his lips

edges.about: whether contemplation is tantamount to speech, both reading it off the same mishna

edges.cueHe: דאי סלקא דעתך הרהור כדבור דמי — יוציא בשפתיו
edges.about: were contemplation equal to speech the impure man would utter Shema outright, so it is not

edges.cueHe: אלא מאי הרהור לאו כדבור דמי, למה מהרהר?
edges.about: if contemplation is not speech, why does the mishna have him contemplate at all

edges.cueHe: אמר רבי אלעזר: כדי שלא יהו כל העולם עוסקין בו והוא יושב ובטל
edges.about: he contemplates so as not to sit idle while everyone else is occupied with Shema
if idleness is the whole concern, let him study some other chapter instead of Shema

edges.cueHe: אמר רב אדא בר אהבה: בדבר שהצבור עוסקין בו
edges.about: he should be occupied with the very matter the community is occupied with

edges.cueHe: ותנן: היה עומד בתפלה ונזכר שהוא בעל קרי
edges.about: the mishna about one who remembers mid-prayer that he is impure

edges.cueHe: והרי תפלה, דדבר שהצבור עסוקין בו, ותנן
edges.about: prayer too is a matter the community is engaged in, yet the impure man may not begin it

edges.cueHe: טעמא דאתחיל, הא לא אתחיל — לא יתחיל
edges.about: the reason is only that he had already begun; had he not begun he would not begin, even by contemplation

edges.cueHe: שאני תפלה דלית בה מלכות שמים

edges.cueHe: והרי ברכת המזון לאחריו דלית בה מלכות שמים, ותנן

edges.cueHe: ותנן על המזון מברך לאחריו ואינו מברך לפניו

edges.cueHe: אלא: קריאת שמע וברכת המזון דאורייתא, ותפלה דרבנן
edges.about: the true line is Torah law against rabbinic law — Shema and Grace after Meals are from the Torah, prayer is rabbinic
